selectionBoundary: The sources define transaction atomicity, persistence assumptions, rollback-resistant update state, key continuity, transparency proofs, and cross-view monitoring. RC51 does not propose a new database, signature scheme, transparency log, gossip protocol, or software-update framework. It tests an application-specific composition for research-event lineage under process termination and backup rollback.

sources.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.usedFor: All-or-nothing transaction semantics and the explicit dependence on filesystem, VFS, operating-system, and hardware behavior.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That this RC51 process-termination schedule is a power-loss or torn-sector test, or that an older complete backup is detectable locally.

sources.title: Write-Ahead Logging
sources.usedFor: WAL commit records, reader snapshots, checkpoint behavior, and same-host scope.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Cross-host consensus or atomic commitment across two independent database files.

sources.title: PRAGMA synchronous
sources.usedFor: The meaning of synchronous=FULL in WAL mode and the distinction between application-crash and power-loss durability.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That the underlying Windows storage stack honors every requested flush under physical failure.

sources.title: How To Corrupt An SQLite Database File
sources.usedFor: The requirement to use the backup API or another consistent snapshot method rather than copying a live database file.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Semantic freshness of a correct old backup.

sources.title: Node.js SQLite documentation
sources.usedFor: DatabaseSync and the SQLite backup API used by the Node implementation.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Application policy correctness or interoperability with a production service.

sources.title: RFC 9162: Certificate Transparency Version 2.0
sources.usedFor: Merkle consistency, signed tree heads, the split-view limitation, and the need for clients to compare views to detect equivocation.
sources.doesNotEstablish: A complete gossip protocol or physical truth of logged statements.

sources.title: Sigstore Rekor logging overview
sources.usedFor: Operational log auditing and named independent-monitor implementations.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That RC51's two local processes have independent administration or production Rekor semantics.

sources.title: Sigstore Security Model
sources.usedFor: The boundary that long-term transparency trust requires monitoring and that users retain responsibility for monitoring unauthorized identities.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That a signature or an unmonitored local tree head is globally fresh.

sources.title: The Update Framework Specification
sources.usedFor: Persisted trusted version state, exact N+1 root rotation, dual old/new threshold signatures, and rollback, freeze, and mix-and-match checks.
sources.doesNotEstablish: That TUF version rules automatically apply to experimental-event lineage; RC51 makes and tests that transfer explicitly.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Revision 5: Recommendation for Key Management
sources.usedFor: Key lifecycle, cryptoperiod, compromise, backup, archive, and trust-anchor terminology.
sources.doesNotEstablish: An RC51 key-custody audit; all keys in this cycle are public deterministic demonstration keys.

sources.title: RFC 9942: Concise Binary Object Representation (CBOR) Object Signing and Encryption (COSE) Receipts
sources.usedFor: Inherited RC50 receipt boundary: a receipt authenticates a specific statement and proof context.
sources.doesNotEstablish: One-time nonce use, latest-state semantics, or uniqueness across logs.

sources.title: RFC 9943: An Architecture for Trustworthy and Transparent Digital Supply Chains
sources.usedFor: Inherited RC50 signed/transparent-statement architecture and relying-party policy boundary.
sources.doesNotEstablish: Physical provenance accuracy or the RC51 persistent application state machine.

repositoryInheritance.inherited: Event identity, domain separation, and first-appearance boundary.
repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC51 does not rerun the eighty single-fault identity trials.

repositoryInheritance.inherited: Forty-four frozen composite cases, locally valid rollback/fork counterexamples, and the stateful reset-bridge result.
repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC51 does not enlarge or regenerate the RC50 fixture corpus and does not rerun its CBOR/COSE wire vectors.

repositoryInheritance.inherited: Crash placement around commit and the distinction between local state, delivery evidence, and externally owned effects.
repositoryInheritance.notRepeated: RC51 targets causal-lineage freshness, key epoch, and backup restoration rather than claiming exactly-once remote actuation.

noveltySearch.provisionalDifference: RC51 combines well-known transactional state, TUF-like version/key continuity, and CT-like view comparison for a specific scientific-event causal tuple. The combination is an experiment-specific policy transfer, not a new primitive.
